title: Recursion · Understanding and Tracing
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: True or false? A Student borrowing a Book is normally an inheritance relationship.
questions.feedback: False. Borrowing is an association: a Student is not a kind of Book.

questions.prompt: In Book(string title), what is title?
questions.feedback: A parameter received by the constructor.

questions.prompt: Values A, B and C are pushed onto a stack in that order. Which is popped first?
questions.feedback: C. A stack is last in, first out.

questions.prompt: A function AddTwo(x) returns x + 2. Calculate AddTwo(AddTwo(3)).
questions.feedback: The inner call returns 5; the outer call returns 7.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: recursion — A function calling itself to solve a smaller problem.
base case — A condition that stops further recursive calls.
recursive case — A call to the same function with a smaller or simpler input.
call stack — Memory holding active function calls and their local values.
return value — The result passed back to the caller.

blocks.title: Independent practice
blocks.text:
State two features of a terminating recursive function.

Trace SumTo(3), giving the value returned by each call.
function SumTo(n)
    if n == 0 then
        return 0
    endif
    return n + SumTo(n - 1)
endfunction

Explain why the call stack is needed during recursion.

questions.prompt: What is the final return of SumTo(3) with base case 0 returning 0?
Which call returns first in Factorial(4)?
What happens to active calls as they return?
questions.answer: They are removed from the call stack.
options: They are removed from the call stack.
questions.feedback: Model answer: They are removed from the call stack.
Recursion involves a function calling itself.

questions.prompt: A base case must make another recursive call.
questions.feedback: The base case returns without making another call.

questions.prompt: Each active recursive call has its own stack frame.
questions.feedback: Each frame stores that call’s own parameters, local values and return information.
